speakers: Jim kasang (volatility / options market-structure specialist, Chicago)
Niels costr Larson (host, hedge fund manager)
summary: Early August 2024 weekly systematic-investor show. Jim explains volatility supply pinning the index, the July-August 2024 unpinning via call-gamma unwind and Nvidia/Russell rotation, and why positioning in vol supply matters. He also argues Trump 2.0 (tariffs, immigration limits, activist Fed) is inflationary, that wealth effects make the Fed reactive to markets, and gives a path view: fall wobble, rally into year end.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: I still wonder whether we are seeing still way too calm reaction in the financial markets to what's really
claims.claim: Financial markets reacted too calmly to the escalating Middle East conflict in early August 2024.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: July turned out to really be a month in 3x we had act one which was very strong start for Trend followers
claims.claim: July 2024 trend following was strong in the first 10 days, then narratives and data shifted and trends reversed in a rotation.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: that was super challenging with large correction across most markets in particular us Japanese equities energies
claims.claim: From 10 to 25 July large reversals hit equities, energies, metals, grains and currencies together, a typical trend-follower drawdown from a simultaneous change of direction.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer finished the month at 48 so that does suggest of a neutral flat plus minus a couple of percent month
claims.claim: A Trend barometer reading of 48 maps to a roughly flat month for the trend industry; July 2024 CTA indices ended about -1.6% to -2.5%, year to date +5% to +6%.
claims.indicator: Trend barometer; SG CTA index; BTop50

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: World Government Bond index was up 1.78% so clearly benefited from this shift in narratives
claims.claim: Government bonds rose 1.78% in July 2024 as growth and rate narratives shifted, while equities were up about 1.7% (MSCI World) and S&P 500 about 1.25%.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: the last streak we had of a magnitude like that occurred in 2017 and 2018 leading into vaget
claims.claim: The S&P 500 ended a 356-day streak without a 2% decline on 24 July 2024; the previous comparable streak (351 days) ended in the Volmageddon of early 2018.
claims.testable: yes - streak-length versus later vol is testable but few episodes

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: there's so much reflexivity to the system that when V is offered and well supplied uh we get these periods of immense unconscious like like
claims.claim: When option volatility is heavily sold and well supplied, reflexive dealer hedging pins index volatility and produces very calm index behaviour (two months without a 50bp decline in summer 2024).
claims.testable: partly - supply is hard to measure

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: once that ball becomes unpinned then it reflexively now accelerates volatility and with all the zero DTE things that we're seeing
claims.claim: After a long pinned period, once volatility unpins the move is larger because dealer and zero-DTE flows reinforce selling and buying (as after 2017's record low realised vol).

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the whole year we didn't have a decline greater than 3% lowest Vol realized volatility in history in 2017
claims.claim: 2017 had no decline above 3% and the lowest realised volatility in history, followed by a bigger vol break in 2018.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the strength and and uh positioning in that V Supply especially as we go out in time right is so critical to the system
claims.claim: Positioning in volatility supply across expiries (weak in September-November 2024) shows where the system is fragile; weak forward supply means a small unpinning can start a larger move.
claims.indicator: volatility supply by expiry (VIX / options positioning)
claims.conditions: when forward-month vol supply is thin

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: if you uh are able to manage both the timing uh element U as you know as we focus on um as well as uh you know look at the relative value opportunities
claims.claim: Long-vol returns are wide-ranging; passive put buying lost more than it made, while skill in timing leverage up/down and in relative-value (dispersion, cross-index) pays.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: it is not an asset class as people like to call it you know it it is really the underlying distribution across all asset classes
claims.claim: Volatility is not an asset class but the underlying distribution of all asset classes, so vol-market dynamics drive broad market performance.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: if you blindly just go buy the same put every day for 50 years or the long and you will lose money
claims.claim: Mechanically buying the same puts loses money over the long run since options are insurance, but the case for it is geometric return benefit under rebalancing.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: when the Market's down and you make a you know convexly and you make a bunch of money it's counter correlated to everything else and so you can monetize it and put that money to work in the market
claims.claim: Put payoffs in market falls can be monetised and reinvested via rebalancing, turning a negative standalone return into positive portfolio geometric growth.
claims.indicator: portfolio with put overlay and rebalancing

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the edge that I think is most valuable is understanding positioning in the
claims.claim: The edge in systematic put buying is positioning (dealer/vol supply) used as a timing and sizing signal, combined with relative-value cheapness.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: the Barkley hedge volatility trading index which as far as I understand comprises of 23 funds
claims.claim: The Barclay Hedge Volatility Trading index (23 funds, +3% end of June 2024) was found as a benchmark; Jim prefers more specific Cboe strategy indexes to benchmark vol managers.
claims.indicator: BarclayHedge Volatility Trading index; Cboe indices

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: mechanism and a sizing mechanism to leverage on and leverage off
claims.claim: Positioning serves as timing and sizing mechanism to leverage long-vol up and down where the distribution has most risk.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: returns are not incredibly high but they dramatically help your geometric returns
claims.claim: A volatility allocation has modest standalone return but a large geometric-return benefit at portfolio level, so it should be a systematic part of the portfolio.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: carry trades by definition are convex when they break and there's an argument to be made that the majority of the market is a carry trade
claims.claim: Carry trades have positive expectancy over the long run but break convexly; short-skew option positions are carry trades that earn nine times out of ten.
claims.conditions: fail suddenly when crowded and leveraged

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: puts are more expensive than calls there is a a relative value trade there that you can make money nine times out of 10
claims.claim: Selling puts, buying calls and selling stock earns the skew premium most of the time because puts are richer than calls, at the cost of a dramatic tail.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the Yen carry trade is incredibly convex and it works and it works and it works
claims.claim: The dollar-yen carry trade pays steadily but if you are still in when it breaks you can lose everything in days or weeks; hedges are linear and crowded.
claims.direction: short JPY carry, risk when unwinding

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: if things really start to break you know the government will be there to kind of try and bail people out
claims.claim: Investors accept carry-trade tails because they expect policy backstops, which is part of why carry makes money over the long run.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: macro what's happening that can drive bigger structural changes on a multi-year basis
claims.claim: Jim's framework: combine macro (multi-year structural distribution and incentives) with flows/market microstructure to align short, medium and long term.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: if Trump wins he's going to win the Senate they already hold the house
claims.claim: If Trump wins in 2024 he would likely also take the Senate and keep the House, giving a broad mandate; the Supreme Court immunity ruling adds executive scope.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: protectionism immigration policy activist fed um are all not only um inflationary but they are very bullish together
claims.claim: Tariffs/protectionism, immigration restriction and an activist Fed are each inflationary and together bullish for hard assets; a hot economy favoured over global growth.
claims.conditions: Trump wins and executes the agenda

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: closing the Border We Believe will will dramatically accelerate in uh labor inflation um here
claims.claim: Open borders were a release valve for US labour-market inflation; closing them is expected to accelerate labour inflation.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: that are um really diversifications um to the dollar and to uh inflation
claims.claim: Gold and Bitcoin are diversifiers against the dollar and inflation in a Fed-activism scenario.
claims.conditions: dollar debasement or Fed loses independence

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: in the US's best interest um to tax the world
claims.claim: In the short term US power plays (tariffs, activist Fed) benefit the US relative to the world, but over time they degrade trust in the system, a positive-short-term convex-tail outcome.
claims.conditions: short term benefits, long term costs

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: it actually at the moment is pretty loose it's very accommodative when you look at this index
claims.claim: The Chicago Fed financial conditions index (including credit spreads) showed conditions loose in mid 2024 despite high policy rates, per Jim Grant.
claims.indicator: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: it is triggered if there is a rise of 50 basis points or more in the 3 months average compared to the low of the last 12 months
claims.claim: Sahm rule: a 0.5 pt rise of the 3-month average unemployment rate above its 12-month low signals recession; the host suspects the July 2024 4.3% print triggered it.
claims.indicator: Sahm rule on US unemployment rate

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: there's a wealth effect which people call which I I I cannot emphasize this enough is way bigger and way more important to the outcomes of the macro picture than more or less anything other than the Federal Reserve
claims.claim: The wealth effect from equity and equity-linked collateral (about $200 trillion) is the most important macro driver after the Fed, so a 10% fall removes about $20 trillion of collateral.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the whole policy engine is a focus of offsetting and trying to manage the market
claims.claim: The Fed is reflexive to markets because market collateral moves money supply, which is why Powell signalled action if markets did something weird; expect Fed to react to a market fall.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: they said okay we're going to cut we're going to do six cuts the market repriced market went up 20% and guess what economic outcomes were way better than people expected
claims.claim: The December 2023 dovish repricing lifted equities 20% and improved growth, showing easy financial conditions feed back into the economy.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the FED has to be very Nimble and quick to react as a function of Market action
claims.claim: The Fed can reverse from cutting to tightening and back quickly (late 2018) depending on market action, so expect a policy turn if markets stay down into Jackson Hole.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: if they go up 50 basis points versus down 50 basis points it's not a linear effect always on economic outcomes
claims.claim: Rate hikes had slow effects because households locked in rates and demand was sequestered; lowering rates now releases accumulated demand, so cuts may have a larger effect than hikes.
claims.indicator: Fed funds rate changes, mortgage lock-in

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the second you lower interest rates now you release uh that demand uh and and it can really accelerate demand
claims.claim: In a demand-push economy (1970s analogy, with money going to individuals not corporations) lowering rates re-releases demand and inflation spikes back after recessions, so the Fed cannot easily manage inflation.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the oil shocks the geopolitical uh conflict are a function of protectionism
claims.claim: Protectionism and America First raise geopolitical conflict, oil shocks and fiscal spending, so more oil and copper supply control is expected, a supporting factor for commodities.

claims.speaker: Niels costr Larson
claims.quote: is in the midst of a two-day decline that is the biggest since 2011 the tsunami in 2011
claims.claim: Japan's Topix had its largest two-day decline since 2011 in early August 2024, a wealth-effect shock alongside a flight to safety into bonds.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the Japanese have been on this road a lot longer than we have and they will go buy stocks
claims.claim: Japanese authorities intervene in equity markets directly because they recognise the wealth effect; a US analogue is possible.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: that Divergence when it gets to this extreme can itself cause underlying volatility
claims.claim: Index calm held together by vol supply masks extreme single-stock dispersion; extreme dispersion can itself force stress back into the index.
claims.indicator: dispersion between stocks versus index vol
claims.conditions: extreme dispersion with low index vol

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: momentum in Nvidia specifically and broadly in those Tech names started to slow
claims.claim: The 2024 decline began when momentum in Nvidia and AI tech slowed on idiosyncratic news.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: when that started to slow those calls start to Decay those dealers who are short those calls and long stock now have to start right selling that stock back out
claims.claim: When speculative call buying on AI names slows, dealers short calls and long stock must sell the stock as call delta decays, producing a slow persistent decline.
claims.direction: stock selling as call gamma decays

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the index itself is now going to enforce a greater volatility once a move happens
claims.claim: Because index vol is pinned, a rotation of money from one set of names to others forces index vol higher once a move starts.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the amount of call open interest skyrocketed in the week and a or two weeks before the Russell took off
claims.claim: Surge in Russell call open interest (large upside call purchase) preceded the small-cap rally, spreading the call-gamma squeeze from AI to Russell.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: there is not a single company in the United States that has more to lose if China invades Taiwan
claims.claim: Nvidia carries Taiwan invasion tail risk; a Trump comment that Taiwan should pay for defence changed the narrative and exposed the run to other risks.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: a four standard deviation four standard deviation move
claims.claim: The Russell moved about four standard deviations relative to the S&P after the narrative change.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: what creates volatility and stress is when risk gets concentrated and leveraged into a part of the system
claims.claim: Volatility comes from concentrated, leveraged risk held by a few hands; unwinding big winners in a rotation raises that concentration.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: skew is very very low here FYI
claims.claim: In August 2024 skew was low so tail protection was cheap; historically skew falls during declines as investors sell puts, but a convex move makes skew explode (Volmageddon).
claims.conditions: after decline starts, skew can mean-revert up

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the relative move up in the S&P just two days ago uh a 2% plus move is classic short squeeze
claims.claim: A 2%+ rally during stress with weak action elsewhere is read as a short squeeze, not a recovery.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the V Supply which has been very strong here is fragile
claims.claim: Vol supply can disappear into the November election and a new president, so the calm of summer will not necessarily be there later; stay cautious through September-November.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: my view to be clear has always been slow summer wobble in the fall uh rally back likely sometime early next year the real fireworks begin
claims.claim: Jim's path: calm summer, volatile fall wobble, rally into year end, bigger fireworks in early 2025; the unpinning came a month earlier than planned.

claims.speaker: Jim kasang
claims.quote: the biggest reaction is the Fed right the second one is uh policy in terms of election
claims.claim: The two biggest drivers of path change are the Fed reaction function (50 bp cut or strong language at Jackson Hole) and election policy.
